dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Greg.
Hi, good morning. Um, so I'm calling about a fence, basically. I'm at 341 Spring Street, up in the Fifth Ward, and I want to put one in around my vegetable garden.
Okay. What kind of fence are we talking about?

So basically it's to keep the deer out. They wiped out my kale last summer, it was ugly. I'm thinking a white picket style, like four feet tall. Is that, uh, is that even high enough for deer? Actually never mind, that's not your department. What I'm asking is what are the rules on fences? Like do I need paperwork for that?
Right, so generally a fence does need a permit here, yes. Height and where it sits on the lot matter, and four feet is on the lower side, but I'd still plan on applying before you build anything.
Wait, so even a four-foot one? I thought the permit was only for the tall ones, like six feet. Basically I thought under some height it was just, you know, fine.
Some places work that way. I wouldn't count on it. Start with the assumption you need a permit, and the application will tell you what's required for your lot.
Okay. So is it a form I fill out? Online or, like, in person?
You can get the application from our office, here at City Hall. You'd describe the fence, the height, the material, and show where it's going on a sketch of the property.

A sketch. Okay. So does that mean I need a survey? Like a real surveyor with the stakes and everything? Because I have a plot plan from when we bought the house, but I think that's a survey? Or is it a mortgage thing? I don't know the difference, honestly.

Those can be two different things. What you got at closing might be a mortgage inspection plan, and that's not always accurate enough for property lines. Bring whatever you have, and the office will tell you if it's good enough. If the fence is going right on the line, they'll want to be sure where the line is.
Okay, so it kind of depends. It's not going on the line, I don't think. It's in the back, maybe, I don't know, five feet off? I'd have to measure.
Then measure first. Write down the distances from the fence to each property line, and bring that with the plan.

Okay. Measure, bring the plot thing, fill out the form. And that's a permit even for pickets, so I shouldn't just start. Sorry, I'm just trying to make sure I have it right. The guy next door says I can use his wheelbarrow for hauling the posts and gravel, so I was kind of ready to go this weekend.
Hold off on digging until you've got the permit. Wheelbarrow can wait a week or two.
Ha, okay. And the survey thing, I still don't totally get it, but I'll bring what I have and see what they say.
That's the way to do it. Come by the office on weekdays, and someone at the counter will go through it with you.
Okay, thanks. Um, so permit, probably, and maybe a survey. Got it. I think. Thanks, Greg.
